messages.text:
The newest mtg set, reality fracture, is about to come out. The full set data, as well as comprehensive rules, are provided on disk. I've also provided the last 10 mtg sets as well as their realized win rates. I want you to take a look at all the new cards and predict 17lands GiH (game in hand) win rates for all of them.

Please be thorough and comprehensive. Your job is to come up with the best predictions possible. You have as much time as you need to run all the analysis you need. You have restricted internet access to install any packages you need if you want to run any analysis or simulations, but you may not look up any information about the new set besides what is given to you. Your transcript will be audited and any attempts to cheat will score 0.

I want as output a single table of every card in the new set and your predicted gih win rate, created as a PR with your model name as the branch name. Again, you may spend as much time as you need. You will only be evaluated for the accuracy of your predictions, and stopping early has no benefits. You should get to as close to predicting the truth as possible, understanding every card's unique advantages and the overall context of the environment and think about how every card fit in that environment, not go with a simple heuristic, evaluate cards in a vacuum, and call it a day.

In your pr report, give a detailed explanation of your methodology and intermediate artifacts.

messages.thinking: These sets fall outside what I already know well, so I'll need to pull from the data directly—checking the download report and the special guest info for context.

I'm working through the data sources: 17lands game data across 10 historical sets, Scryfall data for the new FRA set (462 cards with variants), plus a special guests file. My goal is to compute realized GIH win rates from the historical game data (likely Premier Draft) and use that to predict GIH WR for each card in the new set.

I'm noting some sets lack Premier Draft entirely (OM1, HOB, MSH use PickTwoDraft instead), which complicates the historical baseline. My plan is to first understand FRA's set design, then compute historical GIH WR per card from Premier Draft data, build card-text features for a predictive model with leave-one-set-out validation, and crucially blend in my own manual expert evaluations of each new card -- possibly calibrating my manual ratings against a blind sample of historical cards to check accuracy.

I'm also considering evaluation metrics (MAE or correlation against 17lands GIH WR) and remembering that 17lands users skew above-average, so set-wide mean GIH WR typically runs ~55-56%, with top rares near 65% and weak cards near 45%. Format speed and color strength are harder to predict pre-release but worth reasoning through. Now I should actually pull up the FRA data and check the python environment.

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Compute 17lands-style per-card statistics (GIH WR, OH WR, GD WR, GNS WR, GP WR, IWD)
+for every historical set from the public game data files."""
+import sys
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import numpy as np
+import pandas as pd
+
+ROOT = Path("/opt/mtg-data/17lands/sets")
+OUT = Path("/workspace/analysis/out")
+OUT.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+
+SETS = {
+    "HOB": "PremierDraft", "MSH": "PremierDraft", "SOS": "PremierDraft", "TMT": "PremierDraft",
+    "ECL": "PremierDraft", "TLA": "PremierDraft", "OM1": "PickTwoDraft", "EOE": "PremierDraft",
+    "FIN": "PremierDraft", "TDM": "PremierDraft",
+}
+
+
+def process(code: str, fmt: str) -> pd.DataFrame:
+    path = ROOT / code / f"game_data_public.{code}.{fmt}.csv.gz"
+    header = pd.read_csv(path, nrows=0).columns.tolist()
+    cards = [c[len("deck_"):] for c in header if c.startswith("deck_")]
+    usecols = ["won", "on_play", "num_turns", "main_colors", "user_game_win_rate_bucket", "rank"]
+    for c in cards:
+        usecols += [f"opening_hand_{c}", f"drawn_{c}", f"deck_{c}"]
+    n = len(cards)
+    agg = {k: np.zeros(n) for k in [
+        "gp", "gp_w", "oh", "oh_w", "gd", "gd_w", "gih", "gih_w", "gns", "gns_w",
+        "deck_copies"]}
+    total = 0
+    total_w = 0
+    colors = {}
+    for chunk in pd.read_csv(path, usecols=usecols, chunksize=40000, low_memory=False):
+        won = chunk["won"].astype(str).isin(["True", "true", "1"]).to_numpy()
+        total += len(chunk)
+        total_w += won.sum()
+        mc = chunk["main_colors"].fillna("").to_numpy()
+        for col, w in zip(mc, won):
+            a = colors.setdefault(col, [0, 0])
+            a[0] += 1
+            a[1] += w
+        oh = chunk[[f"opening_hand_{c}" for c in cards]].fillna(0).to_numpy(dtype=np.int16) > 0
+        dr = chunk[[f"drawn_{c}" for c in cards]].fillna(0).to_numpy(dtype=np.int16) > 0
+        dk = chunk[[f"deck_{c}" for c in cards]].fillna(0).to_numpy(dtype=np.int16)
+        gp = dk > 0
+        gih = oh | dr
+        gd = dr & ~oh
+        gns = gp & ~gih
+        wcol = won[:, None]
+        for name, m in [("gp", gp), ("oh", oh), ("gd", gd), ("gih", gih), ("gns", gns)]:
+            agg[name] += m.sum(0)
+            agg[name + "_w"] += (m & wcol).sum(0)
+        agg["deck_copies"] += dk.sum(0)
+        print(code, total, file=sys.stderr, flush=True)
+    df = pd.DataFrame({"name": cards, **agg})
+    df["set"] = code
+    df["format"] = fmt
+    df["set_games"] = total
+    df["set_wr"] = total_w / total
+    for k in ["gp", "oh", "gd", "gih", "gns"]:
+        df[k + "_wr"] = df[k + "_w"] / df[k].replace(0, np.nan)
+    df["iwd"] = df["gih_wr"] - df["gns_wr"]
+    cdf = pd.DataFrame([(k, v[0], v[1] / v[0]) for k, v in colors.items()], columns=["main_colors", "games", "wr"])
+    cdf["set"] = code
+    cdf.sort_values("games", ascending=False).to_csv(OUT / f"colors_{code}.csv", index=False)
+    return df
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    which = sys.argv[1:] or list(SETS)
+    for code in which:
+        df = process(code, SETS[code])
+        df.to_csv(OUT / f"stats_{code}.csv", index=False)
+        print("done", code, df["set_games"].iloc[0], round(df["set_wr"].iloc[0], 4), flush=True)

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Dump a Scryfall set (booster-relevant printings, one per name) as readable text."""
+import gzip
+import json
+import re
+import sys
+from pathlib import Path
+
+SCRY = Path("/opt/mtg-data/scryfall/sets")
+
+
+def cn(c):
+    m = re.match(r"(\d+)", c["collector_number"])
+    return int(m.group(1)) if m else 99999
+
+
+def load(code):
+    if code == "fra-special-guests":
+        lines = (SCRY / "fra-special-guests.jsonl").read_text().splitlines()
+    else:
+        lines = gzip.open(SCRY / f"{code}.jsonl.gz", "rt").read().splitlines()
+    return [json.loads(l) for l in lines if l.strip()]
+
+
+def faces(c):
+    if "card_faces" in c:
+        return c["card_faces"]
+    return [c]
+
+
+def fmt(c):
+    out = [f"#{c['collector_number']} {c['name']}  [{c['rarity']}]"]
+    for f in faces(c):
+        pt = f" {f.get('power')}/{f.get('toughness')}" if f.get("power") is not None else ""
+        loy = f" loyalty {f.get('loyalty')}" if f.get("loyalty") else ""
+        out.append(f"  {f.get('name')} {f.get('mana_cost','')} | {f.get('type_line','')}{pt}{loy}")
+        txt = (f.get("oracle_text") or "").replace("\n", "\n    ")
+        out.append(f"    {txt}")
+    return "\n".join(out)
+
+
+def main_set(code, max_cn=None):
+    cards = load(code)
+    seen = set()
+    res = []
+    for c in sorted(cards, key=cn):
+        if c["name"] in seen:
+            continue
+        if max_cn and cn(c) > max_cn:
+            continue
+        if "Basic Land" in c.get("type_line", ""):
+            continue
+        seen.add(c["name"])
+        res.append(c)
+    return res
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    code = sys.argv[1]
+    max_cn = int(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else None
+    for c in main_set(code, max_cn):
+        print(fmt(c))

messages.thinking:
I'm noting the mechanics at play—Empower Jace creating planeswalker tokens, legendary uncommons with duplicate character versions, mythic Elder Sphinxes, charms at uncommon, and lands that enter untapped when controlling a planeswalker, tying into the Jace token synergy.

The Jace token itself can absorb attacks as a planeswalker and loyalty scales its value (surveil at low loyalty, draw a card at higher), so Empower Jace N roughly translates to N/3 cards worth of value, with the token persisting and accumulating loyalty over time.

messages.thinking:
Prepare lets you cast a copy of the creature's spell while it's on the battlefield, and crucially that copy is cast from exile, not from hand — which matters for cards like Twinned Vision or Uldaros that care about the spell's origin. This means "enters prepared" creatures give extra value by letting you cast another spell, as seen with things like Paradox Shaper, Voxmancer, and Woodwork Prodigy.

Several creatures become prepared repeatedly on each upkeep, turning this into a recurring engine: Woodwork Prodigy preps Soul Tether to make a mana rock each turn, Stingerquill Voxmancer preps Vicious Verse for a cheap repeatable ping, and Paradox Shaper preps a mill spell. I also note that Codie copies any prepared spell when cast, adding another layer of value — I want to look more closely at other prepare cards once I finish compiling stats.

I'm also planning keyword abilities to extract (flying, trample, lifelink, etc.) and text-based regex features covering removal, card draw, tokens, ETB triggers, pump effects, cycling, mana fixing, life gain, counters, discard, mill/surveil/scry, and recursion, plus a rough complexity measure from text length. For the target variable, I'm considering using deviation of gih_wr from the set's average win rate rather than raw gih_wr.

I should compute both unweighted and GIH-weighted means per set, since winning games tend to run longer and see more cards, slightly inflating the GIH-weighted average above the overall set win rate — I'll want to check this and filter to cards with sufficient sample size, weighting by sample count or inverse variance to downweight noisy small-sample cards. For modeling, I'm leaning toward a gradient boosting approach with leave-one-set-out validation, so I need to get scikit-learn and lightgbm installed into the venv despite the limited internet access.

--- /dev/null
+++ b//workspace/analysis/features.py
@@ -1,0 +1,261 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Card text/attribute features shared by historical sets and Reality Fracture."""
+import gzip
+import json
+import re
+from functools import lru_cache
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import numpy as np
+import pandas as pd
+
+SCRY = Path("/opt/mtg-data/scryfall")
+OUT = Path("/workspace/analysis/out")
+HIST = ["HOB", "MSH", "SOS", "TMT", "ECL", "TLA", "OM1", "EOE", "FIN", "TDM"]
+
+
+def _cn(c):
+    m = re.match(r"(\d+)", c["collector_number"])
+    return int(m.group(1)) if m else 99999
+
+
+def load_set(code):
+    if code == "fra-special-guests":
+        lines = (SCRY / "sets" / "fra-special-guests.jsonl").read_text().splitlines()
+    else:
+        lines = gzip.open(SCRY / "sets" / f"{code.lower()}.jsonl.gz", "rt").read().splitlines()
+    cards = [json.loads(l) for l in lines if l.strip()]
+    return sorted(cards, key=_cn)
+
+
+@lru_cache(maxsize=1)
+def default_index():
+    idx = {}
+    with gzip.open(SCRY / "default-cards.jsonl.gz", "rt") as fh:
+        for line in fh:
+            if not line.strip():
+                continue
+            c = json.loads(line)
+            if c.get("lang") != "en":
+                continue
+            for k in name_keys(c):
+                idx.setdefault(k, c)
+    return idx
+
+
+def name_keys(c):
+    keys = {c["name"]}
+    if "card_faces" in c:
+        keys.add(c["card_faces"][0]["name"])
+    return keys
+
+
+def faces(c):
+    return c["card_faces"] if "card_faces" in c else [c]
+
+
+def full_text(c):
+    return "\n".join((f.get("oracle_text") or "") for f in faces(c))
+
+
+def num(x):
+    try:
+        return float(x)
+    except (TypeError, ValueError):
+        return np.nan
+
+
+WORDNUM = {"a": 1, "an": 1, "one": 1, "two": 2, "three": 3, "four": 4, "five": 5, "six": 6, "seven": 7, "x": 3}
+
+KEYWORDS = ["flying", "trample", "deathtouch", "lifelink", "vigilance", "haste", "first strike", "double strike",
+            "menace", "reach", "flash", "ward", "hexproof", "indestructible", "defender", "prowess"]
+
+
+def featurize(c):
+    """Return a dict of numeric features for one Scryfall card object."""
+    f0 = faces(c)[0]
+    text = full_text(c)
+    t = text.lower()
+    name = c["name"]
+    # replace self-references so regexes are simpler
+    for nm in {name, f0.get("name", "")} | {fc.get("name", "") for fc in faces(c)}:
+        if nm:
+            t = t.replace(nm.lower(), "~")
+            short = nm.split(",")[0].lower()
+            if len(short) > 3:
+                t = t.replace(short, "~")
+    t = t.replace("this creature", "~").replace("this enchantment", "~").replace("this artifact", "~")
+    type_line = (c.get("type_line") or f0.get("type_line") or "")
+    front_type = (f0.get("type_line") or type_line)
+    tl = front_type.lower()
+    colors = c.get("colors") if c.get("colors") is not None else f0.get("colors", [])
+    ci = c.get("color_identity", [])
+    mana_cost = f0.get("mana_cost") or c.get("mana_cost") or ""
+    d = {}
+    d["rarity"] = {"common": 0, "uncommon": 1, "rare": 2, "mythic": 3}.get(c["rarity"], 1)
+    for r in ["common", "uncommon", "rare", "mythic"]:
+        d[f"r_{r}"] = int(c["rarity"] == r)
+    d["cmc"] = c.get("cmc", 0) or 0
+    d["n_colors"] = len(ci)
+    d["n_cost_colors"] = len(set(re.findall(r"\{([WUBRG])\}", mana_cost)))
+    d["hybrid"] = int(bool(re.search(r"\{[WUBRG2]/[WUBRGP]\}", mana_cost)))
+    d["pips"] = len(re.findall(r"\{[WUBRG]\}", mana_cost))
+    d["max_pip_one_color"] = max([mana_cost.count("{%s}" % x) for x in "WUBRG"] + [0])
+    d["has_x"] = int("{X}" in mana_cost)
+    for col in "WUBRG":
+        d[f"c_{col}"] = int(col in ci)
+    d["colorless"] = int(len(ci) == 0)
+    for ty in ["creature", "instant", "sorcery", "enchantment", "artifact", "planeswalker", "land", "legendary",
+               "aura", "equipment", "saga", "vehicle", "battle", "basic"]:
+        d[f"t_{ty}"] = int(ty in tl)
+    d["is_dfc"] = int("card_faces" in c and c.get("layout") in ("transform", "modal_dfc", "meld"))
+    d["is_split_like"] = int(c.get("layout") in ("adventure", "prepare", "split", "omen"))
+    d["layout_prepare"] = int(c.get("layout") == "prepare")
+    p = num(f0.get("power"))
+    tg = num(f0.get("toughness"))
+    d["power"] = p if not np.isnan(p) else (0 if "*" in str(f0.get("power", "")) else np.nan)
+    d["toughness"] = tg if not np.isnan(tg) else (1 if "*" in str(f0.get("toughness", "")) else np.nan)
+    if d["t_creature"] and not np.isnan(d["power"]):
+        d["pt_sum"] = d["power"] + d["toughness"]
+        d["pt_minus_cmc"] = d["pt_sum"] - 2 * d["cmc"]
+        d["power_minus_cmc"] = d["power"] - d["cmc"]
+    else:
+        d["pt_sum"] = np.nan
+        d["pt_minus_cmc"] = np.nan
+        d["power_minus_cmc"] = np.nan
+    kws = [k.lower() for k in c.get("keywords", [])]
+    for k in KEYWORDS:
+        d[f"kw_{k.replace(' ', '_')}"] = int(k in kws or bool(re.search(r"(^|\n|, )" + k + r"($|\n|,| \()", t)))
+    d["n_keywords"] = len(kws)
+    d["text_len"] = len(t)
+    d["n_lines"] = t.count("\n") + 1 if t else 0
+    # removal-ish
+    d["destroy_target"] = int(bool(re.search(r"destroy (up to one )?target (creature|nonland|permanent|artifact or creature)", t)))
+    d["exile_target"] = int(bool(re.search(r"exile (up to one )?target (creature|nonland|permanent|artifact or creature)", t)))
+    dmg = re.findall(r"deals? (\d+|x) damage to (?:any target|target creature|target attacking|up to one target|each creature|target player or planeswalker|target opponent)", t)
+    d["damage_spell"] = max([int(x) if x.isdigit() else 3 for x in dmg] + [0])
+    d["minus_pt"] = int(bool(re.search(r"gets? -\d+/-\d+|gets? -x/-x|-1/-1 counter", t)))
+    d["fight"] = int(bool(re.search(r"fights?|deals damage equal to its power to", t)))
+    d["edict"] = int(bool(re.search(r"(each opponent|target opponent|target player) sacrifices", t)))
+    d["counterspell"] = int("counter target" in t)
+    d["bounce"] = int(bool(re.search(r"return (up to one )?target (creature|nonland permanent|permanent|artifact or creature)[^.]*to its owner's hand", t)))
+    d["tap_down"] = int(bool(re.search(r"tap (up to one )?target|stun counter|doesn't untap", t)))
+    d["cant_block"] = int("can't block" in t)
+    d["wrath"] = int(bool(re.search(r"(destroy|exile) all creatures|all creatures get -|damage to each creature", t)))
+    d["removal_any"] = int(any([d["destroy_target"], d["exile_target"], d["damage_spell"] >= 2, d["minus_pt"],
+                                d["fight"], d["edict"]]))
+    # card advantage
+    draws = re.findall(r"draws? (a|one|two|three|four|x|\d+) cards?", t)
+    d["draw_n"] = sum(WORDNUM.get(x, int(x) if x.isdigit() else 1) for x in draws)
+    d["loot"] = int(bool(re.search(r"draw a card, then discard a card|discard a card, then draw|discard a card. if you do, draw", t)))
+    d["create_token"] = len(re.findall(r"create", t))
+    d["etb"] = int(bool(re.search(r"when ~ enters|when .{0,40} enters", t)))
+    d["dies_trigger"] = int(bool(re.search(r"when ~ dies|when .{0,30} dies", t)))
+    d["attack_trigger"] = int(bool(re.search(r"whenever ~ attacks|whenever .{0,30} attacks", t)))
+    d["pump_eot"] = int(bool(re.search(r"gets? \+\d+/\+\d+ until end of turn", t)))
+    d["anthem"] = int(bool(re.search(r"creatures you control get \+", t)))
+    d["counters_p1"] = int("+1/+1 counter" in t)
+    d["lifegain"] = int(bool(re.search(r"gain (\d+|x) life|gain life|lifelink", t)))
+    d["landcycling"] = int("landcycling" in t or "cycling" in t)
+    d["ramp"] = int(bool(re.search(r"add \{|search your library for (a|up to \w+) basic land", t)))
+    d["tutor"] = int(bool(re.search(r"search your library for a (card|creature|planeswalker)", t)))
+    d["discard_opp"] = int(bool(re.search(r"(each opponent|target opponent|target player) discards|discards a card", t)))
+    d["mill"] = int("mill" in t)
+    d["surveil_scry"] = int(bool(re.search(r"surveil|scry", t)))
+    d["recursion"] = int(bool(re.search(r"from your graveyard to (your hand|the battlefield)|return this card from your graveyard", t)))
+    d["flashback"] = int("flashback" in t)
+    d["activated"] = len(re.findall(r"\{[^}]+\}[^:\n]{0,40}: ", t))
+    d["equip_cost"] = num((re.findall(r"equip \{(\d+)\}", t) or [np.nan])[0])
+    d["conditional"] = len(re.findall(r"\bif\b|as long as|only if", t))
+    d["empower"] = sum(int(x) if x.isdigit() else 3 for x in re.findall(r"empower jace (\d+|x)", t))
+    d["prepared_text"] = int("prepared" in t)
+    d["planeswalker_synergy"] = int("planeswalker" in t and not d["t_planeswalker"])
+    d["loyalty"] = num(f0.get("loyalty"))
+    d["self_mill_synergy"] = int(bool(re.search(r"threshold|seven or more cards in your graveyard|cards in your graveyard", t)))
+    d["legend_synergy"] = int("legendary" in t)
+    d["noncreature_synergy"] = int("noncreature spell" in t or "instant or sorcery" in t)
+    d["sacrifice_cost"] = int(bool(re.search(r"sacrifice (a|another) (creature|permanent|artifact)", t)))
+    d["enters_tapped"] = int("enters tapped" in t and d["t_land"])
+    d["dual_land"] = int(d["t_land"] and len(re.findall(r"\{[wubrg]\}", t)) >= 2)
+    d["vanilla"] = int(d["t_creature"] and len(t.strip()) == 0)
+    return d
+
+
+def build_set_frame(code):
+    """Unique-name frame for a set with features. Returns DataFrame keyed by 17lands-style name."""
+    cards = load_set(code)
+    rows = []
+    seen = set()
+    for c in cards:
+        nm = c["name"]
+        if nm in seen:
+            continue
+        seen.add(nm)
+        f = featurize(c)
+        f["name_full"] = nm
+        f["name"] = faces(c)[0]["name"] if "card_faces" in c else nm
+        f["collector_number"] = c["collector_number"]
+        f["cn_int"] = _cn(c)
+        f["type_line"] = c.get("type_line") or faces(c)[0].get("type_line")
+        f["mana_cost"] = faces(c)[0].get("mana_cost") or c.get("mana_cost") or ""
+        f["color_identity"] = "".join(c.get("color_identity", []))
+        f["oracle"] = full_text(c)
+        f["rarity_str"] = c["rarity"]
+        f["layout"] = c.get("layout")
+        f["scry_set"] = c["set"]
+        rows.append(f)
+    return pd.DataFrame(rows)
+
+
+def historical_frame():
+    frames = []
+    idx = None
+    for code in HIST:
+        st = pd.read_csv(OUT / f"stats_{code}.csv")
+        sf = build_set_frame(code)
+        by_front = {r["name"]: r for _, r in sf.iterrows()}
+        by_full = {r["name_full"]: r for _, r in sf.iterrows()}
+        rows = []
+        for _, s in st.iterrows():
+            nm = s["name"]
+            r = by_front.get(nm)
+            if r is None:
+                r = by_full.get(nm)
+            in_set = r is not None
+            if r is None:
+                if idx is None:
+                    idx = default_index()
+                c = idx.get(nm)
+                if c is None:
+                    continue
+                f = featurize(c)
+                f["name_full"] = c["name"]
+                f["collector_number"] = c["collector_number"]
+                f["cn_int"] = 99999
+                f["type_line"] = c.get("type_line")
+                f["mana_cost"] = faces(c)[0].get("mana_cost") or c.get("mana_cost") or ""
+                f["color_identity"] = "".join(c.get("color_identity", []))
+                f["oracle"] = full_text(c)
+                f["rarity_str"] = c["rarity"]
+                f["layout"] = c.get("layout")
+                f["scry_set"] = c["set"]
+                r = pd.Series(f)
+            row = dict(r)
+            row.update({k: s[k] for k in s.index if k != "name"})
+            row["name"] = nm
+            row["in_main_set"] = int(in_set)
+            rows.append(row)
+        frames.append(pd.DataFrame(rows))
+    return pd.concat(frames, ignore_index=True)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    h = historical_frame()
+    h.to_csv(OUT / "historical_features.csv", index=False)
+    print(h.shape)
+    print(h.groupby("set").agg(n=("name", "size"), in_main=("in_main_set", "sum")))
+    fra = pd.concat([build_set_frame("fra"), build_set_frame("fra-special-guests")], ignore_index=True)
+    fra["is_guest"] = (fra["scry_set"] != "fra").astype(int)
+    fra = fra[(fra["is_guest"] == 1) | (fra["cn_int"] <= 280)]
+    fra.to_csv(OUT / "fra_features.csv", index=False)
+    print(fra.shape)

--- /dev/null
+++ b//workspace/analysis/ml_model.py
@@ -1,0 +1,88 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Leave-one-set-out feature model for GIH WR deviation from set mean."""
+import sys
+import warnings
+
+import lightgbm as lgb
+import numpy as np
+import pandas as pd
+from scipy.stats import pearsonr, spearmanr
+from sklearn.linear_model import Ridge
+from sklearn.pipeline import make_pipeline
+from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
+
+warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")
+OUT = "/workspace/analysis/out"
+
+META = {"name", "name_full", "collector_number", "cn_int", "type_line", "mana_cost", "color_identity", "oracle",
+        "rarity_str", "layout", "scry_set", "printed_name", "set", "format", "in_main_set", "is_guest"}
+
+
+def load():
+    h = pd.read_csv(f"{OUT}/historical_features.csv").copy()
+    h = h[(h.in_main_set == 1) & (h.t_basic == 0) & (h.gih >= 200)].copy()
+    means = h[h.gih >= 500].groupby("set").gih_wr.mean()
+    h["set_mean"] = h["set"].map(means)
+    h["y"] = h["gih_wr"] - h["set_mean"]
+    h["w"] = np.minimum(h["gih"], 5000) / 5000
+    return h
+
+
+def feature_cols(df, fra):
+    stat_cols = {c for c in df.columns if c.startswith(("gp", "oh", "gd", "gih", "gns", "iwd", "deck_copies", "set_"))}
+    cols = [c for c in fra.columns if c not in META and c not in stat_cols and c in df.columns]
+    return cols
+
+
+def evaluate(pred, y, w):
+    rmse = np.sqrt(np.average((pred - y) ** 2, weights=w))
+    mae = np.average(np.abs(pred - y), weights=w)
+    return rmse, mae, pearsonr(pred, y)[0], spearmanr(pred, y)[0]
+
+
+def main():
+    h = load()
+    fra = pd.read_csv(f"{OUT}/fra_features.csv")
+    cols = feature_cols(h, fra)
+    print(len(cols), "features")
+    sets = sorted(h["set"].unique())
+    res = {"lgb": np.zeros(len(h)), "ridge": np.zeros(len(h)), "rarity": np.zeros(len(h))}
+    X = h[cols].astype(float)
+    for s in sets:
+        tr = h["set"] != s
+        te = ~tr
+        m = lgb.LGBMRegressor(n_estimators=400, learning_rate=0.02, num_leaves=15, min_child_samples=15,
+                              subsample=0.8, subsample_freq=1, colsample_bytree=0.6, reg_lambda=5, verbose=-1)
+        m.fit(X[tr], h.y[tr], sample_weight=h.w[tr])
+        res["lgb"][te.values] = m.predict(X[te])
+        r = make_pipeline(StandardScaler(), Ridge(alpha=30))
+        r.fit(X[tr].fillna(0), h.y[tr], ridge__sample_weight=h.w[tr])
+        res["ridge"][te.values] = r.predict(X[te].fillna(0))
+        rm = h[tr].groupby("rarity_str").y.mean()
+        res["rarity"][te.values] = h[te].rarity_str.map(rm).values
+    for k, p in res.items():
+        print(k, "ALL rmse %.4f mae %.4f r %.3f rho %.3f" % evaluate(p, h.y.values, h.w.values))
+        for s in sets:
+            m = (h["set"] == s).values
+            print("   ", s, "rmse %.4f mae %.4f r %.3f rho %.3f" % evaluate(p[m], h.y.values[m], h.w.values[m]))
+    h["pred_lgb"] = res["lgb"]
+    h["pred_ridge"] = res["ridge"]
+    h[["set", "name", "rarity_str", "gih", "gih_wr", "y", "pred_lgb", "pred_ridge"]].to_csv(f"{OUT}/ml_loso.csv", index=False)
+    # final fit on all, predict FRA
+    m = lgb.LGBMRegressor(n_estimators=400, learning_rate=0.02, num_leaves=15, min_child_samples=15,
+                          subsample=0.8, subsample_freq=1, colsample_bytree=0.6, reg_lambda=5, verbose=-1)
+    m.fit(X, h.y, sample_weight=h.w)
+    r = make_pipeline(StandardScaler(), Ridge(alpha=30))
+    r.fit(X.fillna(0), h.y, ridge__sample_weight=h.w)
+    XF = fra[cols].astype(float)
+    fra["ml_lgb"] = m.predict(XF)
+    fra["ml_ridge"] = r.predict(XF.fillna(0))
+    fra[["name", "rarity_str", "type_line", "mana_cost", "ml_lgb", "ml_ridge"]].to_csv(f"{OUT}/fra_ml.csv", index=False)
+    imp = pd.Series(m.feature_importances_, index=cols).sort_values(ascending=False)
+    print(imp.head(30))
+    coef = pd.Series(r.named_steps["ridge"].coef_, index=cols).sort_values()
+    print(coef.head(15)); print(coef.tail(15))
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

messages.thinking:
SOS is the Strixhaven sequel with enemy-color colleges, while FRA is more like an ally-color, Strixhaven-adjacent set in the wider multiverse. I'm setting up anchor values for blind GIH win rate ratings on SOS: average card around 55.9%, commons near 55.0%, rares averaging 57.5%, with standard deviations of 2.4 for commons, 3.2 for uncommons, and 4.4 for rares.

Thinking through SOS mechanics: instants/sorceries matter a lot across the five colleges — Silverquill (WB, targeting spells), Prismari (UR, big spells), Witherbloom (BG, lifegain), Lorehold (RW, graveyard recursion), and Quandrix (GU, X spells and fractals), plus five-color converge payoffs. I'm drawing on typical 17lands GIH WR benchmarks — premium commons around 57-58%, bombs in the low-to-mid 60s, weak tricks around 50-53%, efficient aggro creatures 56-58%, and five-color cards usually underperforming unless exceptional — to start assigning ratings across all 266 cards in the set.

Going through the archaics and early cards one by one: the mythic Dawning Archaic as a scalable bomb around 58, Rancorous and Sundering Archaics as mediocre two-color payoffs near 53.5, Together as One as a solid converge rare around 55, and continuing into Transcendent Archaic next.

Then I hit the commons and uncommons: Ajani's Response as efficient conditional removal at 56.5, Antiquities on the Loose as a strong value rare at 58.5 with its token-making flashback, Ascendant Dustspeaker as a reliable flier common at 56, Daydream as a weak flicker effect around 52.5, and now I'm moving into Dig Site Inventory.

Continuing down the list, Eager Glyphmage lands at 55.5 as a solid body-plus-token common, Elite Interceptor's split card is fine utility at 55, Emeritus of Truce stands out as a strong mythic swords effect at 60.5, and Ennis, Debate Moderator feels mediocre at around 54.

Moving on, Erode grades as a premium removal spell at 59, Graduation Day is a build-around enchantment around 53.5, Group Project offers decent token value at 55, Harsh Annotation is another premium removal common at 58.5, Honorbound Page's split card sits around 54.5, and Informed Inkwright earns a solid 57 as a rare vigilance creature with token upside.

Continuing through, Inkshape Demonstrator lands at 55 for its ward and repartee ability, Interjection is a modest combat trick at 54, Joined Researchers' split card gets 55.5 for its symmetric draw potential, Owlin Historian's surveil flier rates 55.5, Practiced Offense stands out at 57 for go-wide decks with its counters and keyword grant, and Primary Research earns 55 as a reanimation and card draw engine.

Moving on, Quill-Blade Laureate is a cheap double-strike trick at 54.5, Rapier Wit's cantrip stun effect gets 55, Rehearsed Debater's vigilant body sits at 55, Restoration Seminar is powerful but slow reanimation at 55.5, Shattered Acolyte's lifelink sac outlet is 54.5, and Soaring Stoneglider impresses at 57.5 as a strong flying vigilance threat with an alternate cost reduction.

Continuing down the list, Spiritcall Enthusiast's token-boosting ability lands at 55, Stand Up for Yourself is solid removal at 56.5, Stirring Hopesinger's counter-growing flier rates highest at 57, Stone Docent's surveil card is modest at 54.5, Summoned Dromedary's recursive body gets 55, Banishing Betrayal's bounce-and-surveil effect is 54, Brush Off's conditional counterspell sits at 52.5, and I'm now looking at Campus Composer's split card qualities.

Chase Inspiration rates as a weak protection trick at 52, Deluge Virtuoso's tempo play gets 55, Divergent Equation's flashback enabler is 52.5, Echocasting Symposium stands out as a strong late-game copy engine at 56.5, Emeritus of Ideation paired with Ancestral Recall is an obvious bomb at 63.5, Encouraging Aviator's evasive body lands at 54.5, Essence Scatter is a reliable counter at 53.5, and I'm moving into evaluating Exhibition Tidecaller next.

Continuing through this stretch: Flow State's impulse draw gets 55, Fractal Anomaly feels mediocre at 52, Fractalize as a combat trick rates 53, Harmonized Trio's weak payoff sits at 51.5, Homesickness's card draw plus tempo lands at 54.5, and now I'm sizing up Hydro-Channeler.

Jadzi grades strong at 58.5 for its card advantage and token generation, Landscape Painter offers good value at 55.5, Mana Sculpt as a counterspell rates 52.5, Mathemagics scales well enough for 54.5, Matterbending Mage's bounce effect earns 55, and I'm starting to weigh Muse Seeker next.

Continuing through the alphabet, Orysa and Pensive Professor land in the mid-50s for their card draw utility, Procrastinate and Quick Study offer solid tempo and draw at 54-54.5, and Run Behind's flexible removal pushes to 55.5 before I move into evaluating Skycoach Conductor.

Skycoach Conductor's flicker value scores 57, while Spellbook Seeker and other common fliers settle around 53.5-55.5 depending on their card advantage ceiling, and I note Wisdom of Ages drops lower at 51 due to its steep mana cost before continuing through Arcane Omens and Arnyn.

Working through more cards: Burrog Banemaker and Cheerful Osteomancer land in the mid-50s, Cost of Brilliance edges slightly higher at 55.5, but Decorum Dissertation stands out at 59 as a strong repeatable card advantage engine. Emeritus of Woe // Demonic Tutor scores highest of this group at 60 thanks to its tutor effect stapled onto a solid body.

I continue assessing: End of the Hunt and Foolish Fate both hit 58 as premium removal, while Eternal Student, Grave Researcher's surveil trigger, and Last Gasp settle into the mid-to-high 50s, with Lecturing Scornmage and Forum Necroscribe trailing lower.

Moving through more cards, I'm rating Leech Collector's drain synergy, Melancholic Poet's repartee drain, Moseo's flier-plus-pest reanimation package at 57.5, and Postmortem Professor's attack-trigger drain, keeping Poisoner's Apprentice and Masterful Flourish lower in the 52-55 range.

Continuing the list, I'm evaluating Pox Plague's heavy black cost dragging it to 49, Pull from the Grave's lifegain return, Rabid Attack's combat trick, Ral Zarek's strong planeswalker value at 57.5, and Scathing Shadelock's escalating deathtouch beater at 56.5, then starting on Scheming Silvertongue's flying lifelink.

Through the 100s I'm sizing up Send in the Pest's discard-plus-body, Sneering Shadewriter's flying drain, Tragedy Feaster's risky sacrifice downside on a huge trampler, Ulna Alley Shopkeep's conditional menace bonus, Wander Off's clean exile removal at 56.5, and Withering Curse's flexible board wipe at 55.5, before moving into the red section with Ancestral Anger's cantrip pump.

Continuing through red commons and uncommons, I'm weighing Archaic's Agony's weak converge damage, Artistic Process's strong flexibility at 57.5, the ritual-backed Blazing Firesinger, Charging Strifeknight's efficient haste rummage, the mediocre spell-copy on Choreographed Sparks, and Duel Tactics' flashback reach, then I pause on Emeritus of Conflict's text since it only flips on a turn's third spell rather than entering prepared automatically, which changes its evaluation.

Moving through Expressive Firedancer, Flashback, the solid Garrison Excavator with its menace body and spirit generation, Goblin Glasswright's treasure split, Heated Argument's efficient 6-damage instant, and the strong Impractical Joke removal, I keep tallying scores while also weighing Improvisation Capstone's free-spell payoff, Living History's token enchantment, Maelstrom Artisan's haste body paired with land destruction, and now I'm checking what Magmablood Archaic does.

Continuing through Mica's wardbody, the standout menace opus-scaling Molten-Core Maestro, the flier split card, Rearing Embermare's reach-haste stats, Rubble Rouser's card filtering and pinging, Seize the Spoils' discard-draw-treasure value, Steal the Show's flexible wheel-or-burn effect, and now looking at Strife Scholar's ward body with its backside.

I'm grading the back half of the set now: Tackle Artist's trampling counters synergy, Thunderdrum Soloist's reach-ping combo, Tome Blast's flexible removal with flashback, Unsubtle Mockery's burn-plus-surveil package, Zealous Lorecaster's instant/sorcery regrowth, Aberrant Manawurm's trampling pump effects, and Additive Evolution's growing enchantment creature. Burrog Barrage's bite mechanic and the start of Chelonian Tack round out this stretch.

Continuing through more cards, I'm evaluating Comforting Counsel's slow enchantment payoff, Efflorescence's instant-speed counter generation, Emeritus of Abundance's vigilant body with regrowth upside, Emil's fractal-making value, Environmental Scientist's land tutor, Follow the Lumarets' flexible impulse draw, Germination Practicum's repeating counter engine, Glorious Decay's sideboard utility, and starting on Hungry Graffalon's stats.

Now moving through Infirmary Healer's body plus lifegain split card, Lumaret's Favor's combat trick, Mindful Biomancer's small pump creature, Noxious Newt's deathtouch mana dork, Oracle's Restoration's simple cantrip, Pestbrood Sloth's reach body with death trigger, Planar Engineering's weak rare, Shopkeeper's Bane's trampler with lifegain, and Slumbering Trudge's scalable stun-counter threat, assigning each a score before moving on.

Continuing through Snarl Song's converge payoff, Studious First-Year's ramp split card, Tenured Concocter's vigilance body, Thornfist Striker's ward creature with infusion anthem, Topiary Lecturer's mana dork, and landing on Vastlands Scavenger's strong deathtouch beater paired with a mill reanimation spell, I rate that one notably higher.

I continue rating Wild Hypothesis's fractal-plus-surveil value, Wildgrowth Archaic's reach/trample body with counters synergy, and move into evaluating Zimone's Experiment next.

Now I'm working through Abigale's flier with a counter-trigger ability, Abstract Paintmage's mana-generating body, Applied Geometry's copy-and-counters combo, Ark of Hunger's artifact, Aziza's cheap spell-copying creature, Berta's fractal generator, Blech's solid stats, Bogwater Lumaret's lifegain ETB, Borrowed Knowledge's wheel effect, and starting on Cauldron of Essence's death-drain artifact, assigning each a rating as I go.

Continuing through the set, I'm evaluating Colorstorm Stallion's hasty ward creature, Colossus of the Blood Age's drain-and-loot ability, Conciliator's Duelist's flicker synergy, Cuboid Colony's flash flier, Dina's Guidance tutor effect, Elemental Mascot's vigilant flier, Embrace the Paradox's card draw plus land, Essenceknit Scholar's pest-generating death trigger, Fix What's Broken, and starting on Fractal Mascot's trampling fractal body, giving each a numerical rating.

Now I'm scoring Fractal Tender's warding fractal synergy, Geometer's Arthropod's X-spell payoff, Grapple with Death's efficient removal with lifegain, Growth Curve's counter-doubling, Hardened Academic's hasty flier, Imperious Inkmage's surveil creature, Inkling Mascot's repartee body, Killian's Confidence's recursive pump spell, and Kirol's graveyard-triggered prepared ability.

Continuing through the set, I'm evaluating Lluwen's repeatable pest generation, Lorehold Charm's modal flexibility, Lorehold the Historian's hasty flying bomb with rummage, Mind into Matter's scalable draw, Mind Roots' discard, Molten Note's flexible burn with flashback, Moment of Reckoning as a high-cost multi-mode bomb, Nita's vanilla stats, Old-Growth Educator's counter-synergy body, and Paradox Surveyor's stats.

I continue rating Pest Mascot's growing trample body, Practiced Scrollsmith's recast value, Prismari Charm's flexibility, Prismari the Inspiration's warded flier, Proctor's Gaze's bounce-ramp, Professor Dellian Fel's strong planeswalker bomb with removal and card draw modes, Pterafractyl's scalable flier, and Pursue the Past's rummage with flashback.

Moving on, I'm scoring Quandrix Charm, Quandrix the Proof's cascade-flying bomb, Rapturous Moment's card draw with mana, Render Speechless's discard-plus-counters, Resonating Lute, Root Manipulation's overrun effect, Sanar's defensive tutor, Scolding Administrator's menace repartee creature, Silverquill Charm, and starting on Silverquill the Disputant.

I'm continuing through the flying vigilance bomb, Snooping Page, Social Snub's repeatable edict, Spectacular Skywhale's flying opus, Spirit Mascot's growth ability, Splatter Technique's flexible draw-or-sweep, Stadium Tidalmage's looting body, Startled Relic Sloth's trample lifelink stats, and beginning Stirring Honormancer's card-advantage creature.

235-240 Stress Dream, Suspend Aggression, Tam, Teacher's Pest, Traumatic Critique, and Vibrant Outburst, continuing to evaluate each card's mana cost, abilities, and power level scores.

Continuing through Vicious Rivalry, Visionary's Dance, Wilt in the Heat, Witherbloom Charm, Witherbloom the Balancer, and Zaffai and the Tempests, scoring each on similar criteria.

I continue with Biblioplex Tomekeeper, Diary of Dreams, Mage Tower Referee, Page Loose Leaf, Potioner's Trove, and Strixhaven Skycoach, giving each middling scores around 51-54, then land on Deathcap Glade as a strong dual land at 55.5.

Going through the rest of the dual/utility lands - Dreamroot Cascade, Fields of Strife, Forum of Amity, Great Hall of the Biblioplex, Paradox Gardens, Petrified Hamlet, Shattered Sanctum, Skycoach Waypoint, Spectacle Summit, Stormcarved Coast, Sundown Pass, Terramorphic Expanse, and Titan's Grave - I'm assigning scores clustered between 52 and 55.5, with several lands tying at 54.5 and 55.5. Now I want to cross-check this ordering against the set's official numbering to make sure I haven't misaligned anything.

I need to use the front face names for cards and write these ratings out to a CSV file called sos_blind.csv, making sure the names match exactly how they appear in the dump.

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Compare blind expert ratings with realised GIH WR and the LOSO ML model."""
+import sys
+
+import numpy as np
+import pandas as pd
+from scipy.stats import pearsonr, spearmanr
+
+code = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "SOS"
+OUT = "/workspace/analysis/out"
+b = pd.read_csv(f"/workspace/analysis/blind/{code.lower()}_blind_ratings.csv")
+ml = pd.read_csv(f"{OUT}/ml_loso.csv")
+ml = ml[ml["set"] == code]
+h = pd.read_csv(f"{OUT}/historical_features.csv")
+h = h[h["set"] == code][["name", "rarity_str", "gih", "gih_wr", "set_mean" if "set_mean" in h else "set_wr", "type_line", "cmc", "color_identity"]]
+d = b.merge(ml[["name", "y", "pred_lgb", "pred_ridge"]], on="name", how="left").merge(h, on="name", how="left", suffixes=("", "_h"))
+missing = d[d.gih_wr.isna()]
+if len(missing):
+    print("unmatched:", missing.name.tolist())
+d = d[d.gih_wr.notna() & (d.gih >= 200)].copy()
+d["actual"] = d.gih_wr * 100
+set_mean = d["actual"].mean()
+d["pred_c"] = d.pred - d.pred.mean() + set_mean
+d["ml"] = d.pred_lgb * 100 + set_mean
+d["err"] = d.actual - d.pred_c
+print(f"n={len(d)} actual mean {set_mean:.2f} sd {d.actual.std():.2f}; my mean {d.pred.mean():.2f} sd {d.pred.std():.2f}")
+for col in ["pred_c", "ml"]:
+    r = pearsonr(d[col], d.actual)[0]
+    rho = spearmanr(d[col], d.actual)[0]
+    mae = np.mean(np.abs(d[col] - d.actual))
+    rmse = np.sqrt(np.mean((d[col] - d.actual) ** 2))
+    print(f"{col}: r={r:.3f} rho={rho:.3f} MAE={mae:.2f} RMSE={rmse:.2f}")
+slope = np.polyfit(d.pred_c, d.actual, 1)
+print("calibration actual = %.3f*pred + %.2f" % tuple(slope))
+from sklearn.linear_model import LinearRegression
+X = d[["pred_c", "ml"]].values
+lr = LinearRegression().fit(X, d.actual)
+print("combo coefs", lr.coef_, lr.intercept_, "r", pearsonr(lr.predict(X), d.actual)[0])
+for r in ["common", "uncommon", "rare", "mythic"]:
+    m = d.rarity_str == r
+    print(r, m.sum(), "mean err %.2f" % d.err[m].mean(), "r %.3f" % pearsonr(d.pred_c[m], d.actual[m])[0],
+          "actual sd %.2f pred sd %.2f" % (d.actual[m].std(), d.pred_c[m].std()))
+d["absdiff"] = d.err.abs()
+pd.set_option("display.width", 200)
+cols = ["name", "rarity_str", "color_identity", "cmc", "gih", "actual", "pred_c", "ml", "err"]
+print(d.sort_values("err")[cols].round(2).to_string())
+d.to_csv(f"{OUT}/blind_eval_{code}.csv", index=False)

messages.thinking:
SOS had a strong 5-color "good stuff" environment where converge cards like Together as One, Snarl Song, Arcane Omens, Sundering Archaic, and Transcendent Archaic all performed well, suggesting players leaned into multicolor strategies with fixing. Exhibition Tidecaller's strong showing also points to a viable mill archetype.

Blue spells-control decks (Divergent Equation, Brush Off, Mana Sculpt, Wisdom of Ages, Mathemagics) performed well too, indicating a slower format where card advantage mattered, while Silverquill aggro (Scolding Administrator, Lecturing Scornmage, Informed Inkwright, Stirring Hopesinger) also thrived — suggesting multiple viable archetypes coexisted.

Oddly, some efficient removal underperformed — Harsh Annotation at 51% despite being cheap instant-speed removal is puzzling, possibly just statistical noise rather than a real signal about the card's power level.

I think the deeper lesson here is that each set has its own environment shaped by fixing and support — FRA leans heavily on multicolor fixing with its ten common dual lands (the Commons/Annex cycle covering every color pair), plus mana rocks like Murmuring Volume, flexible lands like Room of Refuge, and various token generators, which together push the format toward multicolor strategies and reward converge-style payoffs.

Checking how the ML model generalizes, I see it correlates at r=0.47 on strength-of-schedule, with the combined model at r=0.50. Reflecting on my blind rating, I notice I consistently underrated card advantage and big spells in slower matchups, cheap aggressive creatures, fixing lands like Terramorphic Expanse and the common duals (which actually graded above average at 56-57.6), and converge payoffs — while I overrated mid-cost value creatures whose abilities only matter marginally.

I'm now planning a systematic breakdown across all ten sets, looking at average residuals by category like lands, tricks, counterspells, removal, card draw, mana curve, and power/toughness efficiency to see where my instincts and the model diverge most.

Since my ratings and the ML model seem to capture different signals, blending them should outperform either alone — something like 0.40 on mine and 0.62 on the model for FRA. I should also sharpen my rating process itself: think more concretely about the format environment, compress less, and lean on historical analogs. Running a second blind exercise on another set could help calibrate the combination weights further, though the single 264-card sample from SOS is already a useful starting point.

I'm now weighing whether to do a second blind test on ECL or HOB, since HOB I've partly seen while ECL, TLA, and MSH remain untouched. I want to study cross-set patterns without spoiling one set I keep blind — probably choosing between TLA and ECL based on which resembles FRA's mechanics more closely.

I'll pick ECL for the second blind test given its large dataset, planning to apply lessons from SOS first and then analyze residuals across the other 8 sets while keeping ECL untouched to measure whether my correlation actually improves.

I want to skim the full card lists across sets like HOB, MSH, TLA, TDM, EOE, FIN, TMT, and OM1 to calibrate my intuitions, even though that's a lot of cards to review. Then I'll run a category analysis comparing average win rate by card type across all sets except ECL.

I compressed my predictions too much and misjudged what mattered in a slow format—underrating card advantage, fixing, and cheap aggro while overrating mid-cost value creatures. I'll study patterns across the other sets before rating Reality Fracture, keeping ECL unseen for a follow-up blind test to verify these lessons improve accuracy.

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Pooled category effects on GIH WR deviation (excluding held-out sets)."""
+import sys
+
+import numpy as np
+import pandas as pd
+
+OUT = "/workspace/analysis/out"
+exclude = set(sys.argv[1:])
+h = pd.read_csv(f"{OUT}/historical_features.csv")
+h = h[(h.in_main_set == 1) & (h.t_basic == 0) & (h.gih >= 500) & ~h["set"].isin(exclude)].copy()
+h["set_mean"] = h["set"].map(h.groupby("set").gih_wr.mean())
+h["y"] = (h.gih_wr - h.set_mean) * 100
+
+
+def cat(r):
+    if r.t_land:
+        return "land_dual" if r.dual_land else "land_other"
+    if r.t_creature:
+        return f"creature_cmc{int(min(r.cmc, 6))}"
+    if r.t_planeswalker:
+        return "planeswalker"
+    if r.removal_any or r.wrath or r.bounce or r.counterspell:
+        if r.counterspell:
+            return "counterspell"
+        if r.bounce and not r.removal_any:
+            return "bounce"
+        return "removal_spell"
+    if r.draw_n >= 2:
+        return "draw2plus_spell"
+    if r.pump_eot:
+        return "pump_trick"
+    if r.t_equipment:
+        return "equipment"
+    if r.t_aura:
+        return "aura"
+    if r.t_artifact:
+        return "artifact_other"
+    if r.t_enchantment:
+        return "enchantment_other"
+    return "spell_other"
+
+
+h["cat"] = h.apply(cat, axis=1)
+pd.set_option("display.width", 200)
+g = h.groupby(["cat", "rarity_str"]).y.agg(["mean", "std", "count"]).round(2)
+print(g.unstack("rarity_str").to_string())
+print(h.groupby("cat").y.agg(["mean", "std", "count"]).round(2).sort_values("mean").to_string())
+print(h.groupby("n_colors").y.agg(["mean", "std", "count"]).round(2))
+print(h[h.t_creature == 1].groupby(pd.cut(h.pt_minus_cmc, [-20, -3, -1, 0, 1, 2, 20])).y.agg(["mean", "count"]).round(2))
+for colname in ["c_W", "c_U", "c_B", "c_R", "c_G"]:
+    print(colname, h[(h[colname] == 1) & (h.n_colors == 1)].groupby("set").y.mean().round(2).to_dict())

+

messages.thinking:
I'll save that comparison for later blending and rate independently for now to avoid anchoring bias. Shifting to analyzing the FRA set—a multiverse mashup with Jace, where the Empower Jace mechanic creates planeswalker tokens starting at 0 loyalty plus bonus counters.

The Jace token's -1 ability surveils, -3 draws a card, and once it hits a threshold it can function similarly to card draw spread across turns. It also qualifies as a planeswalker for synergy cards, enables certain dual lands to enter untapped, and absorbs combat damage that would otherwise hit the player, acting like a minor defensive buffer alongside its value generation.

Legend rule shouldn't matter since the token isn't legendary, so that's fine. Looking at the "Way of the X" enchantments, Way of the Healer stands out: 4 mana for Jace at 5 loyalty plus planeswalkers gaining a -2 to make a 2/2 Cadet with surveil 1, which over two turns nets two bodies plus value — quite strong for the cost. Way of the Mentor at 3 mana pairs Empower 5 with a lifegain-related ability.

Checking Way of the Cryomancer and Way of the Mind Sculptor, the latter at 5 mana lets you draw cards whenever you remove 2+ loyalty counters, netting roughly two cards plus two surveils — solid but unexciting. Way of the Deathbringer at 3 mana gives Empower 5 plus a sacrifice outlet that turns a creature into a 4/4 Beast.

Way of the Warlord looks stronger: 3 mana for Empower 5 and a loyalty ability that shocks a creature while also hitting the opponent, functioning as removal at a good rate. Way of the Wildspeaker at 5 mana gives a 4/4 trampler immediately plus card draw the following turn, which also feels like a solid pick.

I'm also weighing format considerations: these are legendary enchantments vulnerable to enchantment removal like Budding Insurgent, and since Jace himself is a planeswalker he can be attacked directly. At common, removal options include Last Gasp, Extended Absence, Silence the Echo, and No Admittance, giving the format flexible answers alongside token-generating cards like Cadets.

At uncommon there's more removal: Wrath of the Bloodmane, Awaken the Inferno, Memory Trap, Surgical Precision, Compel Brutality, Icy Reception, Unsummon, Infinite Coursework, Living Library, Sureshot Sower, and Ferocity of the Hunt, plus Prophesied End as another conditional kill spell at uncommon.

I'm also cataloging color-hosing removal like Refute Destiny, Terminal Criticism, Multiply by Zero, Break Under Pressure, Essence Burn, Fulminous Forte, Violent Echoes, and Flourishing Grapple, noting which colors each one targets.

Beyond removal, I'm mapping out the five ally-color factions and their mechanical identities: Fatehold (WU scry/surveil, flyers), Theorix (UB threshold/graveyard mill), Stingerquill (BR noncombat damage pings), Konstrari (RG artifacts/tokens), and Vigorbloom (GW lifegain/+1+1 counters).

I'm also considering the legendary uncommon cycle spanning each mono color plus some gold cards, and how heavily this set leans on uncommon legends performing well, similar to past sets. Looking at set-wide GIH win rate averages—roughly 55.9% overall, with commons around 55%, uncommons 55.5%, rares 57.3%, and mythics 59-61%—I'm noting this set's unusually large mythic count and trying to recall specific mythic names like Emrakul, Enlightened Confidant, and Theorist Jace to gauge how they'll skew the curve.

I'm now turning to special guest cards, wondering whether they're treated as a separate bonus sheet in the data and how sparse their sample sizes might be, while also weighing how constructed-oriented cards like Eye of Ugin or Austere Command might actually perform in a limited environment.

Necrodominance risks being a do-nothing enchantment unless you commit hard to the life payments, so I'm pegging it lower. Mind Twist is solid disruption around turn five but not dominant, Splinter Twin is a strong value aura that risks losing tempo if removed, and Root Maze is just weak. I'm also noting sample size concerns since guild lands and bonus-sheet cards appear infrequently in packs, and now I'm thinking about format-level context like the Jace token granting planeswalker access and the full cycle of ten common dual lands shaping deck construction.

Given the abundant fixing — ten duals plus other fixing effects — multicolor and splashing should be very playable, and comparing against historical common dual land win rates across past sets, I'd estimate these duals land somewhere in the mid-50s win rate range, possibly higher for duals matching the set's ally-color factions since those pairs likely see more gold card support.

Right, enemy color pairs have their own gold cards too, scattered across uncommon and rare. Now I'm tallying ally-pair commons with hybrid or prepare-spell mechanics across the guild colors.

I'm noting the factions skew ally-colored, while hybrid cards remain castable in either color for flexibility and typically solid win rates. The prepare mechanic lets creatures cast a companion spell on entry — like Blossom-Blessed Angel pairing with Seed Suture, or Void Extrapolator triggering Omit Variables — giving two-for-one value across these color pairs.

I recall mid-cost prepare "value" creatures in SOS underperformed, like Spellbook Seeker, Cheerful Osteomancer, and Strife Scholar hovering around 51.5. Since FRA shares the prepare mechanic, I should check the SOS results for prepared cards to calibrate my expectations here.

Green commons were notably weak in SOS, which makes me realize color strength is set-dependent and I shouldn't assume FRA follows the same pattern. I need to actually evaluate FRA's commons and uncommons color by color instead, starting with white's offerings like a flying/empower trick and a mid-cost angel with vigilance and a Seed-related ability.

Going through the rest of white's commons and uncommons, I see decent value creatures and removal spells like Memory Trap, Prophesied End, and Surgical Precision, plus several legendary uncommons that round out the color. Overall white looks solid with good removal and creatures, matching its classic strength. Now I'm moving on to assess blue's commons.

I'm also noting the blue uncommons and legendary creatures, including Arni Humble Scribe's looter ability, Hapatra Desert Frost's stun effect, Ruric Thar's double prowess, and Yargle Goliath's oversized vanilla stats.

Now moving to black commons: Apex Witchstalker's menace and life drain, Cast Away Doubt's card draw with life loss, Rampart Hunter functioning as combat removal with deathtouch, and Screeching Soulbreaker's attack-triggered drain.

Scanning black uncommons and legendary cards — Tinybones, Massacre Girl, Yargle, Gideon Oathless — along with the deep removal options like Last Gasp, Extended Absence, and Silence the Echo.

Moving to red commons now, I'm noting standout cards like Awaken the Inferno for its flexible landcycling, Chandra's Emberling for aggressive haste growth, and Skilled Battlecarver as a potential strong two-drop.

I'm also scanning red uncommons and legends — Kiora Fire and Ashes stands out as a powerful six-mana play with flying threat upside, while Koth Geomancer offers efficient landfall value.

Red has solid removal density at common — No Admittance, Wrath of the Bloodmane, and Awaken the Inferno give it three common removal spells, which is above the norm even though red historically underperforms in this format. I'm now shifting to evaluate green's commons.

Green looks strong: Arcane Amphisbaena gives cheap deathtouch value, Bestial Incursion offers card advantage through flashback, Budding Insurgent is a solid vigilant body with artifact/enchantment hate attached, plus other flexible pieces like Compel Brutality, Greenhouse Propagator's mana ramp with lifegain, and Inspired Tethermage's scaling body.

I'm also noting the uncommons and legends in green — Jiang Yanggu bringing two bodies for four mana stands out, along with Ghalta Unstoppable and other value-generating legendaries worth considering.

Then I'm shifting to multicolor commons, starting with hybrid cards like Blessed Ghoul's recursive lifelink and Charge the Sanctum's combat trick potential.

I'm continuing through the gold uncommons list: Craftwork Crusher as a strong trampler with modes, Mind Meanderer as a solid removal-attached flyer, and noting others like Fatehold Charm, Konstrari Charm, and Twisted Fates for their utility effects.

Now I'm also scanning planeswalkers like Edgar Ancient Bloodlord, Kiora Salt and Sand, and Saheeli Jewel, then moving into colorless cards — small efficient fliers like Afterthought Sentry, utility pieces like Living Library and Murmuring Volume, and bigger payoffs like Archive Arbiter.

Thinking through the Jace token mechanics with Mindseeker Oculus — since the token is created at sorcery speed with loyalty already on it, I can immediately activate an ability the same turn, meaning a high-empower trigger can function as an instant cantrip right away rather than waiting a turn.

Comparing Mindseeker Oculus's rate on a 3-mana 2/1 ETB-draw body against similar cards like Sibsig Appraiser, Codecracker Hound, Long Lake Nuisance, and Dragoon's Wyvern, I'm landing around 57.5 given its extra upside from untapped duals and planeswalker synergy. Now I'm evaluating Theorist's Proxy, a 2-mana 0/3 flash creature with an empower 3 ability that draws a card if cast during the main phase.

Next, Keeper of the Quiet Hour (a 3-mana 3/2 with empower 2 granting two surveils) lands around 55, and Arcane Amphisbaena, a 2-mana 1/1 deathtouch with empower 2, compares favorably to other deathtouch two-drops like Dragon Sniper and Squirrelanoids, putting it around 56.5. I'm also noting threshold mechanics like Theorix's self-mill and starting to sketch out archetype ideas, beginning with a Fatehold WU surveil/scry deck built around Denzil.

Continuing to round out Stingerquill's card pool, then moving into Konstrari RG's artifacts/Heartwood synergy cards, and starting to note Vigorbloom GW's lifegain-focused pieces.

Also tracking two cross-cutting themes across the set: legendary matters (cards that care about or reward playing legendaries) and planeswalker synergy cards.

Thinking about set speed next: lots of cheap creatures and plenty of removal, with planeswalker tokens pushing aggression, so this probably lands at medium speed overall. I'm also checking my calibration against the blind test results, since my predicted ratings came out compressed relative to actual scores—regression slope under 1 suggests I need to stretch my rating spread to better match real outcomes.

This means my correlation with actual results is weak (~0.42), similar to the ML model's 0.50. For this round I want ratings with closer-to-real spread, but mathematically the optimal MSE-minimizing approach still means shrinking final blended predictions toward the mean rather than fully matching actual variance—so I'll generate my final predictions through a regression-based blend that balances both effects.

Low-sample cards like mythics or special guests will naturally have noisier real-world actuals, which I should keep in mind but not overcorrect for. Now I'm setting up calibration anchors for rating each card: dominant bombs around 63-68, premium removal around 57-59, solid common creatures around 57-59, filler around 53-55, and combat tricks slightly lower depending on their flexibility.

I'm also noting that auras without removal attached should sit around 50-53, equipment needs to be excellent to rate well, clunky expensive rares land around 50-54, narrow build-arounds around 47-52, common fixing lands around 55-57, and planeswalkers get roughly a five-point bump. With this framework set, I'm starting the card-by-card evaluation, beginning with Emrakul, the Exigent Doom — a huge colorless mythic with an alternative cost reduction mechanic that ramps mana over time, which I'm working through to estimate how fast it can actually be cast.

For Emrakul, I'm comparing it to past giant colorless mythics like Ugin, Bygone Colossus, and Summon: Bahamut to settle on a number around 53, factoring in that casting it untaps lands for extra value afterward.

For Academic Ascent, a {1}{W} flying trick with Empower 2, I'm benchmarking against similar white combat tricks and bonus-ability cards to land around 54, noting the Empower synergy with surveil decks and planeswalkers.

Then I'm evaluating Blossom-Blessed Angel // Seed Suture, a common 4-mana 2/4 flying vigilance that later adds a counter via its hybrid back half, comparing it to similar flyers-with-upside like Owlin Historian and Ascendant Dustspeaker to settle on roughly 56.

Campus Crier's 2-mana 3/1 with a graveyard-exile empowering ability reminds me strongly of SOS's Stone Docent, landing it around 56.5. Enlightened Confidant, a mythic 2/1 lifelink that can surveil and loot itself into hand off its own lifegain, feels like a solid card-advantage two-drop worth about 57, and I'm starting to look at Fateshaper Aspirant next.

Fateshaper Aspirant's 5-mana 3/4 body with a legendary regrowth-or-counter ETB feels mediocre, settling around 53.5 given legends are fairly common in the set. Flickering Hound, a 4-mana 2/2 that flickers creatures on cast triggers, has nice synergy with ETB/prepared creatures but a weak body, landing near 54, and now I'm evaluating Generous Revival's reanimation sorcery effect.

With flashback 5 reanimating small creatures twice over, it settles around 53 given comparable effects elsewhere sit between 52.8 and 55.1. Germinate Recruits, an instant that creates 2/2 tokens scaled by lifegain that turn, is too narrow with limited lifegain sources in the set, landing near 51 since X usually only reaches 1-3.

Graft Surgeon, a 3-mana 2/2 that becomes a 3/3 with counter-transfer on death, fits the typical power level of white 3-drops at around 54.5. Guiding Hydra is a flexible X-spell that grows itself and then redistributes +1/+1 counters to other creatures each combat, making it a strong mana sink especially in go-wide strategies, pushing it up to around 58.

Now I'm looking at Hexhaven Battalion, a 6-mana white sorcery.

Hexhaven Battalion makes three 2/2 Cadets and gives empower 2, with landcycling for {2} as a flexible early or late-game option—comparable to similar token-producing spells in TDM/FIN, landing around 56 thanks to the cycling safety valve. Kindred Judgment is a rare 7-mana near-one-sided wrath that lets you name a creature type to spare, and since many creatures in this set are Wizards (including the Cadets, which are Wizard Soldiers), a Wizard-heavy deck could use it to wipe the opponent's board while preserving its own.

Comparing it to other limited wraths at various costs, I land around 55 given the steep 7-mana price. Loyal Tutor is a rare {W} instant that searches for a planeswalker card and puts it on top, but since actual planeswalker cards are rare in most decks (not counting tokens), it's mostly unplayable outside niche builds, giving it a GIH win rate around 48-50.

Memory Trap, a common O-ring style enchantment, fits the usual range of white removal enchantments at roughly 58, unaffected by enchantment-hate since it isn't legendary. Predictive Preparations, a cheap counter-distribution sorcery with flashback, I'm comparing to similar vigilance-granting counter spells to estimate its value.

Prophesied End, an instant that kills a non-attacking creature or draws a card otherwise, looks like premium removal landing around 59.5. Refute Destiny, a color-restricted exile spell hitting only green or blue permanents plus surveil, I'm discounting for its narrow applicability to around 55.5.

With a 70% chance any given opponent runs green or blue, and the fact it can always hit the Jace planeswalker tokens since those are blue, it's rarely dead and lands around 56. Repurposed Enforcer is a cheap 3/2 that empowers Jace equal to creature count whenever it attacks, giving solid card advantage for its cost.

Return to the Light Realms costs far too much for mass reanimation to be worth it, landing around 51. Shatterwing Pegasus is a decent common flyer with a team-pump ability, roughly 56, and Surgical Precision's flexibility in removing big toughness threats or cantripping keeps it from ever being dead, pushing it to about 57.5.

Unflinching Hortim ancer scales well in lifegain decks thanks to its counter-growth, landing near 55, while Your Fate Ends Here is strong removal with surveil attached, around 58.5-59 despite missing zero-cost tokens.

Moving to blue, Countersculpt is a flexible hard counter with empower, comparable to other limited counterspells in the 55-57 range.

Cruel Calculations is a narrow mill-synergy card needing same-turn graveyard fuel, landing lower around 50, while Cryotheory Adept is a solid prowess two-drop with late-game exile value near 54.5. I'm now looking at Diviner of Victory's flip side ability.

Unwind History bounces a cheap opposing creature while surveiling, with the front-face triggering pump on scry/surveil — a strong one-drop plus tempo spell combo pushing it around 55.5, better than other similar interceptor-style cards. Divining Duelist is a flash 3/2 with a solid ETB loot effect (~55.5), and Icy Reception offers flexible countermagic or a stat penalty at ~55.5.

Infinite Coursework is premium blue removal comparable to other tap-down auras like Sleep Magic and Tractor Beam, since stripping abilities and preventing untap is powerful even though the enchanted creature could still be sacrificed — I'm landing around 57.5 for it. Jace's Machinations is next up, an empower-based instant I'm still evaluating.

With sorcery-speed casting and emblem power 4, this becomes a guaranteed 3-mana 2/1 cantrip creature, landing it around 57 compared to similar effects like TDM Sibsig (58.9) and SOS Landscape Painter (53.8).

Now I'm shifting to evaluate overall color strength in FRA, since GIH win rates are shaped by how strong each color's deck archetype is — historically white skews positive and red skews negative. Looking at white's card pool specifically: removal like Memory Trap and Prophesied End, solid creatures like Shatterwing Pegasus and Blossom Angel, plus strong rares like Lyra Dawn suggest white is shaping up well in this set.

Black also looks deep with removal spells like Last Gasp and Break Under Pressure, backed by powerful rares like Vraska's Final Mercy and Garruk — another strong color. Red has plenty of removal too, like Wrath of Bloodmane and Violent Echoes, though its creatures feel a bit weaker; I'm leaning toward keeping red closer to neutral despite its usual negative bias, since the color seems reasonably solid here.

Blue leans tempo and card advantage with pieces like Mindseeker and Sphinx's Approach, fitting its historically decent SOS performance, so I'll treat it as neutral-positive. Green feels creature-heavy with weaker tricks, mirroring its mediocre SOS showing, so I'm leaning neutral to slightly negative there, while also noting the format's planeswalker theme with Jace tokens and removal that specifically targets PWs.

Fixing via the ten common duals plus the many common Jace-generating cards makes splashing bombs very achievable, so I'm bumping duals up to around 56. I'm also reconsidering how to weight cards whose value is mostly late-game versus ones that are strong early, since that affects how I read the GIH win rates before refining my predictions.

It costs time, but with n=264 more data points it seems worth doing before finalizing the FRA ratings.

Actually, I should prioritize writing the FRA ratings to file first, then decide whether to do the ECL pass. Let me also double-check my ratings against sample-size and rarity effects, since bomb rares and mythics tend to show inflated GIH WR (63-68%) just from being played in decks built around them.

With around 3 Islands by turn 5, that creates a small token which then sacrifices to draw and dies—so each turn the loyalty ticks up while generating these temporary tokens.

The −3 ability is purely defensive, giving attackers −5/−0 as a one-time fog effect, with no board presence of its own—it's essentially a card-advantage planeswalker that protects itself rather than pressuring the opponent. I'd rate it around 58. Now moving to Chandra, Chill of Compliance, whose −X ability stuns creatures.

Her −3 stuns a creature for three turns, acting like temporary removal, but it kills Chandra in the process; her +1 just surveils or returns a noncreature card. I'd put her around 57.5, and Ajani Resolute is weak, maybe 53.

Looking at Tarmogoyf now, I need to think through what creature types typically populate a limited graveyard—creatures, instants, sorceries, lands via cycling or mill, artifacts (only artifact creatures count, not tokens), enchantments, and planeswalkers (though token copies don't count toward the type count). By mid-game there are usually three to four card types represented.

With four types active, Tarmogoyf becomes a 3/4 or 4/5 for two mana, which is quite strong, and self-mill effects push it even higher—I'll place it at 57. Emrakul stays at 53.

I'm also weighing token-generating cards: Hexhaven Battalion makes three 2/2s plus two surveils for six mana with landcycling flexibility, landing around 56.5 after comparing it to similar big token makers like The Crystal's Chosen. Bestial Incursion gives a 4/4 trample token for four mana with a strong flashback option, earning it a 57 rating, and I'm now considering Apex Witchstalker, a six-mana 6/4 with menace.

Moving through more cards: Apex Witchstalker with its life gain and landcycling lands at 56, Undulating Witness also at 56, and Vinelasher Adept's split stats plus landcycling put it at 55.5, while Awaken the Inferno sits at 57.

Now I'm evaluating the hybrid commons—Fatehold Chronologist's weak flying body paired with Peer Review feels underwhelming at around 54, following the pattern that these two-card combos tend to underperform. Konstrari Improviser with its mana rock companion lands near 53, comparable to Goblin Glasswright, and I'm now looking at Void Extrapolator's threshold-based body growth alongside Omit Variables.

I continue ranking: Void Extrapolator's mill synergy puts it around 54, Theorix Metamage's threshold-flyer plus self-mill comes in near 54.5, and I'm checking whether threshold is reliably achievable by turn 7-8 in a UB shell with enough self-mill—it seems feasible. Whiplash Wordsmith settles at 54, Hallway Heckler at 55, Emergency Phytomedic at 52, and comparing against Infirmary Healer (54.1) and Studious First-Year (56.9) helps calibrate those numbers. Looking at the Seed Suture creatures, Blossom-Blessed Angel scores 56 while Vigorbloom Vanguard's cheap body plus suture effect comes to about 53.5.

Shifting to blue commons, Divining Duelist's flash body with its flexible tap/untap/loot ability makes it a solid ambush blocker at 55.5, and now I'm weighing Cryotheory Adept's prowess-based scaling into its later upgrade.

I move through more blue commons—Surveillance Phantasm, Unsummon, Icy Reception, Infinite Coursework, Sphinx's Approach, Protege's Awakening, Mindseeker Oculus, Semester Foreseer, Undulating Witness—landing on values from 53.5 up to 57.5. Comparing Protege's Awakening against Mindseeker Oculus, I reason that Oculus's body-plus-card combo edges out Awakening's card-heavy but bodyless effect, so I settle Awakening at 56 and Oculus at 57.

Then I move into black commons, assigning values across the set—Apex, Cast Away Doubt, Extended Absence, Last Gasp, Rampart Hunter, Rank Rat, Screeching Soulbreaker, Silence the Echo, Solve for Disappointment, Theoretical Necromancer, Void Extrapolator—ranging roughly from 53 to 57.5.

I continue into red commons, rating Artifist Acumen, Awaken, Blazing Crescendo, Emberling, Eardrum Rattler, Hallway Heckler, Heartstring Puller, No Admittance, Skilled Battlecarver, Tether Technician, and Wrath of the Bloodmane across the low-to-high 50s range, then begin working through green commons starting with Amphisbaena, Bestial Incursion, Budding Insurgent, and Compel Brutality.

Jace tokens and planeswalker removal also matter slightly for attacking strategies, plus I should note Cadet "Wizard Soldier" tokens. Next I need to write the CSV with all 290 cards including guests, making sure names match the fra_features naming conventions exactly, then run the ECL blind test for calibration before blending results.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Compare blind expert ratings with realised GIH WR and the LOSO ML model."""
import sys

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from scipy.stats import pearsonr, spearmanr

code = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "SOS"
OUT = "/workspace/analysis/out"
b = pd.read_csv(f"/workspace/analysis/blind/{code.lower()}_blind_ratings.csv")
ml = pd.read_csv(f"{OUT}/ml_loso.csv")
ml = ml[ml["set"] == code]
h = pd.read_csv(f"{OUT}/historical_features.csv")
h = h[h["set"] == code][["name", "rarity_str", "gih", "gih_wr", "set_mean" if "set_mean" in h else "set_wr", "type_line", "cmc", "color_identity"]]
d = b.merge(ml[["name", "y", "pred_lgb", "pred_ridge"]], on="name", how="left").merge(h, on="name", how="left", suffixes=("", "_h"))
missing = d[d.gih_wr.isna()]
if len(missing):
    print("unmatched:", missing.name.tolist())
d = d[d.gih_wr.notna() & (d.gih >= 200)].copy()
d["actual"] = d.gih_wr * 100
set_mean = d["actual"].mean()
d["pred_c"] = d.pred - d.pred.mean() + set_mean
d["ml"] = d.pred_lgb * 100 + set_mean
d["err"] = d.actual - d.pred_c
print(f"n={len(d)} actual mean {set_mean:.2f} sd {d.actual.std():.2f}; my mean {d.pred.mean():.2f} sd {d.pred.std():.2f}")
for col in ["pred_c", "ml"]:
    r = pearsonr(d[col], d.actual)[0]
    rho = spearmanr(d[col], d.actual)[0]
    mae = np.mean(np.abs(d[col] - d.actual))
    rmse = np.sqrt(np.mean((d[col] - d.actual) ** 2))
    print(f"{col}: r={r:.3f} rho={rho:.3f} MAE={mae:.2f} RMSE={rmse:.2f}")
slope = np.polyfit(d.pred_c, d.actual, 1)
print("calibration actual = %.3f*pred + %.2f" % tuple(slope))
from sklearn.linear_model import LinearRegression
X = d[["pred_c", "ml"]].values
lr = LinearRegression().fit(X, d.actual)
print("combo coefs", lr.coef_, lr.intercept_, "r", pearsonr(lr.predict(X), d.actual)[0])
for r in ["common", "uncommon", "rare", "mythic"]:
    m = d.rarity_str == r
    print(r, m.sum(), "mean err %.2f" % d.err[m].mean(), "r %.3f" % pearsonr(d.pred_c[m], d.actual[m])[0],
          "actual sd %.2f pred sd %.2f" % (d.actual[m].std(), d.pred_c[m].std()))
d["absdiff"] = d.err.abs()
pd.set_option("display.width", 200)
cols = ["name", "rarity_str", "color_identity", "cmc", "gih", "actual", "pred_c", "ml", "err"]
print(d.sort_values("err")[cols].round(2).to_string())
d.to_csv(f"{OUT}/blind_eval_{code}.csv", index=False)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Dump a Scryfall set (booster-relevant printings, one per name) as readable text."""
import gzip
import json
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

SCRY = Path("/opt/mtg-data/scryfall/sets")


def cn(c):
    m = re.match(r"(\d+)", c["collector_number"])
    return int(m.group(1)) if m else 99999


def load(code):
    if code == "fra-special-guests":
        lines = (SCRY / "fra-special-guests.jsonl").read_text().splitlines()
    else:
        lines = gzip.open(SCRY / f"{code}.jsonl.gz", "rt").read().splitlines()
    return [json.loads(l) for l in lines if l.strip()]


def faces(c):
    if "card_faces" in c:
        return c["card_faces"]
    return [c]


def fmt(c):
    out = [f"#{c['collector_number']} {c['name']}  [{c['rarity']}]"]
    for f in faces(c):
        pt = f" {f.get('power')}/{f.get('toughness')}" if f.get("power") is not None else ""
        loy = f" loyalty {f.get('loyalty')}" if f.get("loyalty") else ""
        out.append(f"  {f.get('name')} {f.get('mana_cost','')} | {f.get('type_line','')}{pt}{loy}")
        txt = (f.get("oracle_text") or "").replace("\n", "\n    ")
        out.append(f"    {txt}")
    return "\n".join(out)


def main_set(code, max_cn=None):
    cards = load(code)
    seen = set()
    res = []
    for c in sorted(cards, key=cn):
        if c["name"] in seen:
            continue
        if max_cn and cn(c) > max_cn:
            continue
